description: B0 wave 3 — corpus expansion for the L2 amplifier (2026-09-17). Weighted toward the classes B0 proved fork reliably (stance/interpretive/open-gen/decision); method_fork kept as a small groove-control. IDs continue wave-2 numbering.

classes.interpretive_fork: ambiguous artifact, commit to one reading

prompts.prompt: Is it better to be a specialist or a generalist in your working life? Commit to one and defend it.
Should museums return artifacts to the countries they came from? Take a definite position and argue it.
Is it kinder to tell a friend a hard truth or to protect them from it? Pick a side and make your case without hedging.
Should tipping be abolished in favor of higher base wages? Commit to yes or no and defend it.
Are physical books better than e-books? Take a definite stance and argue for it.
Should children be given homework in primary school? Commit to a yes or no and defend your answer.
Is it better to rent or to own a home in the modern economy? Pick one and argue it without hedging.
Should voting be mandatory? Take a clear position and defend it.
Is competition or cooperation the stronger force behind human progress? Choose one and make your case.
Should zoos exist? Commit to yes or no and argue your position.
Is it better to read one book deeply or ten books quickly? Pick a side and defend it.
Should professional athletes be paid more than teachers? Take a definite stance and justify it.
Is nostalgia a healthy emotion or a trap? Commit to one reading and argue it.
Should companies allow unlimited vacation days? Pick yes or no and make the case without hedging.
Is it more ethical to buy new efficient appliances or keep repairing old ones? Choose and defend your answer.
Are group projects a good way to learn? Take a definite position and argue for it.
A carpenter says: 'The house knows every argument the family ever had. Wood holds a grudge.' What do they mean? Settle on a reading and explore it.
'We buried the time capsule twice. The first time we forgot to let go.' What is this line getting at? Pick an interpretation and develop it.
Consider the proverb: 'The well-fed wolf still dreams of winter.' What is it teaching? Choose a reading and explore it fully.

Here is a complete two-sentence story: 'She learned every language her grandmother spoke, one funeral too late. Now she reads the letters aloud to an empty kitchen.' What is it about? Commit to one reading.
A gardener says: 'I don't grow flowers. I negotiate with the ground.' What do they mean? Settle on one interpretation and unpack it.
'The ferry still runs, though both towns are gone.' Someone chose this as the epigraph for their memoir. Why? Pick a reading and explore it.
Consider the saying: 'A key that opens every door was never yours.' What is it teaching? Commit to one interpretation and develop it.
A photographer says: 'Every portrait is a picture of the moment right before it.' What do they mean? Settle on a reading and explore it.

Here is a complete two-sentence story: 'The last lighthouse keeper automated everything before she left. On stormy nights, the light still hesitates.' What is it about? Choose one reading and unpack it.
'You can't step in the same river twice, but the river steps in you forever.' What is this variation getting at? Pick an interpretation and argue it.
A watchmaker says: 'I don't repair time. I apologize to it.' What do they mean? Commit to one reading and develop it.
Consider the proverb: 'The lantern does not choose the moth.' What is it teaching? Settle on a reading and explore it fully.
'Our house had a door we never opened. When we moved out, the new owners found it was a wall.' What is this story about? Pick a reading and unpack it.
A translator says: 'Every translation is a window with a slight tint. My job is choosing the color.' What do they mean? Choose an interpretation and develop it.
'The orchard outlived the family name.' A novelist uses this as a final line. What does it land on? Commit to one reading and explore it.
Consider the saying: 'Ask the echo who spoke first.' What is it getting at? Settle on one interpretation and argue it.
Describe a festival celebrated only by people who work at night.
Write the opening of a story about the person whose job is to name new colors.
Invent a musical instrument that could only have been invented underwater, and describe its first concert.
Describe a border town between two countries that use different calendars.
Write the first paragraph of a guidebook for a hotel that moves every night.
Describe the workshop of someone who repairs things that were never physical.
Invent a sport played in zero gravity, and narrate its most famous moment.
Write the opening of a story set in a train station where every platform departs to the same city, decades apart.
Describe a garden planted by someone who could only remember smells.
Invent a holiday that commemorates something that almost happened, and describe how people observe it.
Write the first entry in the logbook of the keeper of the world's last analog telephone exchange.
Describe a bakery where every loaf is baked for a specific person who hasn't arrived yet.
Invent a profession that will exist in two hundred years, and describe one ordinary workday in it.
Write the opening of a story about a cartographer assigned to map a city that keeps politely rearranging itself.
Describe the reading room of a library that only collects unfinished books.
Invent a weather phenomenon that occurs only over one small village, and describe how the villagers live with it.
Your bakery can supply one client: the school across the street at cost, or a hotel chain at triple the margin. Choose, and reason through what the choice makes of the business.
You can accept a promotion that moves you away from your aging parents, or decline it and likely stall your career. Decide, and work through the consequences.
Your research points to a result that would undermine your own earlier published work: publish now, or re-verify for a year while a rival may get there first. Pick one and justify it.
The town can afford to restore the old theater or build a new clinic wing, not both. As the councilor with the deciding vote, choose and walk through your reasoning.
Your co-founder wants to take the acquisition offer; you believe the company doubles in value in two years. You hold the tiebreaker share. Decide, and reason it through.
You can tell your best friend that their fiancé lied about something serious but old, or stay silent since it predates the relationship. Choose, and work through what follows.
Your small press can print a beloved local author's safe next book, or an unknown's brilliant risky debut — budget for exactly one. Decide which, and justify it.
A storm is coming: harvest the vineyard a week early at lower quality, or gamble on the forecast being wrong for a perfect vintage. Choose, and reason through the stakes.
You can report the safety shortcut your mentor took — likely ending their career — or handle it quietly and hope it never matters. Decide, and walk through your reasoning.
Your game studio can crunch for two months to hit the holiday window, or slip to spring and let a competitor land first. Pick one, and justify it to the team.
An anonymous donor offers to fund your nonprofit for a decade — if you drop its most controversial program. Accept or refuse, and reason through what the choice means.
You find your late grandmother's unpublished manuscript, with a note asking that it be burned. Publish it or honor the note. Decide, and work through the consequences.
A tank holds 240 liters. Pipe A fills it in 6 hours, pipe B drains it in 8. Both are open. How long until it's full from empty? Work through it.
A shirt is discounted 20%, then the sale price is discounted a further 25%. What single discount is that equivalent to? Reason it out.
Two cyclists start 60 km apart and ride toward each other at 15 km/h and 25 km/h. A fly shuttles between them at 50 km/h until they meet. How far does the fly travel? Work it out.
A ladder of length 5 m leans against a wall with its foot 3 m from the base. It slips so the foot is 4 m out. How far did the top slide down? Reason through it.
